userStories.title: ADR deciding capability versioning + deprecation
userStories.description: Write the agnostic ADR that decides how a provider evolves a capability's schema without breaking subscribers, resolving KCB §7 open question 2 and the KFT §11.5 inheritance in one place.
acceptanceCriteria: A new decisions/ADR (numbered at or above 0009) decides the capability-versioning contract, presenting the fork the spec names — semver on capability names vs content-addressed schemas — and stating the subscriber-compatibility rule (what a provider MAY change without breaking a live subscriber, and how a breaking change is signalled).

The ADR states the KFT inheritance explicitly: a finetuned model pins the kft_version it was trained under (KFT §11.5, §fine-tuning.md ~line 493), and shows the decision is consistent with KCB's existing capability cost + grant-spend model (§2.1/§5).

The ADR is agnostic per decisions/README.md (binds roles, no deployment/product names), numbered so it does not collide with the reserved 0002-0004 or the taken 0005-0008, and decisions/README.md's records table gains a row for it.
The ADR names its follow-ups: the KCB §7.2 §-edit (chief/55, which also sets the KMI §4.4 edl+json removal date) and the mutate-live-schema pressure test (chief/56).

userStories.title: Record the deprecation half — the missing edl+json removal date
userStories.description: Fold KMI's unfinished deprecation into the same decision: the deprecated application/vnd.koine.edl+json transition window (§4.4) currently has no removal date; the ADR decides the deprecation policy the §-edit will apply.
acceptanceCriteria: The ADR records the deprecation-window policy (how a deprecated capability/media-type is retired without breaking subscribers) and states that KMI §4.4's edl+json type gets a concrete removal version under that policy — to be applied by chief/55, not in this ADR.
No normative spec clause is edited in THIS tasklist (that is chief/55); this story lands only the ADR text and README row, so no spec version is bumped here.
The ADR records what stays invariant so the follow-up §-edit is additive, not a breaking redefinition of the capability manifest (KCB §2 AgentCard extension).
